requirements.requirement: Install and configure a file-integrity tool (AIDE) that covers /etc on node1
requirements.summary: aide/aide-common were installed (cmd-3064b113dbe14f9f). The distro default aide.conf.autogenerated already applies a recursive '/ Full' rule at the root (line 950, confirmed in cmd-f765d2d1d48843f5 and cmd-19c1b8efc7a14c9f) that covers /etc contents (the '/etc$ VarDir' rule only anchors the directory entry itself, not its children, so it does not exclude /etc from the root Full rule). The executor's attempt to add an explicit '/etc Full' fragment (cmd-6de572edae9f4ea2) did not actually get incorporated into the generated config (cmd-19c1b8efc7a14c9f grep for '/etc Full' found nothing, and the same command returned exit code 1), so that specific addition was ineffective, but coverage of /etc was already present via the default rule and was independently verified by direct change-detection testing.

requirements.requirement: Build and persist a baseline database that later checks can compare against
requirements.summary: A baseline aide.db (70,163+ entries) was built via aideinit and promoted to /var/lib/aide/aide.db, with creation timestamp and sha256 recorded under /var/lib/aide/baseline-meta/ (cmd-f765d2d1d48843f5, sha256 4503abdf...bda2828). The same sha256 was confirmed present immediately before restart (cmd-03fd5da1c69a4a27) and unchanged immediately after restart (cmd-7aaf06df22744ed9), showing the baseline persists across a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Baseline must be shown to actually detect later changes to /etc (so changes can be identified/reported)
requirements.summary: A test file was created under /etc (/etc/aide-baseline-test.conf) and aide --check against the built database directly flagged it as added ('f++++++++++++++++: /etc/aide-baseline-test.conf', nonzero exit code 7) in cmd-f765d2d1d48843f5; the test file was then removed. Detection was re-verified post-restart with a second test file (cmd-7aaf06df22744ed9), also correctly flagged and cleaned up.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with pre-restart healthy state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered baseline/service state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (35c87ec9...) and clean baseline state were captured (cmd-03fd5da1c69a4a27, cross-checked by fixed global:before_prepare boot-identity observation with the same value). A native reboot was issued and acknowledged (cmd-d5b4787dc8d34f9c), SSH connection dropped, then refused while down (cmd-ff08e57b5556460b), then returned with a new boot_id (615f60f8..., cmd-d05fc38a660f4d21), matching the fixed global:after_executor boot-identity observation. Post-restart, the aide.db sha256 was unchanged and /etc detection still worked (cmd-7aaf06df22744ed9), demonstrating full recovery.

overall_summary: The task's material outcomes — installing AIDE, establishing a baseline covering /etc, and demonstrating that later changes to /etc are detected — are all satisfied with direct, first-hand command evidence (a test file created under /etc was correctly flagged by aide --check, both before and after a restart). Coverage of /etc is real but comes from the distro's default recursive '/ Full' rule rather than the executor's intended explicit '/etc Full' fragment, which appears not to have been incorporated into the built configuration despite being written to disk. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed cleanly: pre-restart boot identity and healthy baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a changed post-restart boot identity (consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and confirmed recovery of the identical baseline database and working change detection.
limitations: The root cause for why the explicit '/etc Full' fragment (50-etc-full-baseline.conf) was not incorporated into the generated aide config was not diagnosed by the executor; it is left in place as inert, unverified configuration.

cmd-eb7f52360d2a4030 returned a proxy timeout rather than a clean exit code, so its exact server-side completion could not be directly confirmed beyond the follow-up log inspection in cmd-6f7dfba6a66f4fbc.
Only a single managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so the provider-wide restart protocol was assessed against that one node only.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two notable unnecessary/ineffective mutations occurred. First, the executor created an ad-hoc /etc-only override config (/etc/aide/aide.conf.d/99-etc-only.conf and aide.conf.orig, part of cmd-3064b113dbe14f9f STEP 2) that was later explicitly removed in cmd-eb7f52360d2a4030 STEP 1 — a bounded, low-risk mutation that was fully reverted. Second, the executor added /etc/aide/aide.conf.d/50-etc-full-baseline.conf intending an explicit '/etc Full' rule (cmd-6de572edae9f4ea2), but evidence shows this fragment was never actually incorporated into the generated aide config (cmd-19c1b8efc7a14c9f) — it remains on disk as an inert, misleading residual file with no confirmed corrective follow-up or removal. This is low-risk (a single benign config line, does not weaken security or break anything) but is unreverted residue whose stated purpose was not achieved. One executor command (cmd-eb7f52360d2a4030) failed with a proxy timeout; the follow-up check (cmd-6f7dfba6a66f4fbc) showed the underlying server-side script had continued and effectively completed, so no orphaned broken state resulted. Test artifacts created for change-detection verification (/etc/aide-baseline-test.conf, /etc/aide-postrestart-test.conf) were both promptly removed.
